backbone: Inbox + Case file. Every role - including the maintenance field reporter, who had no Home in v1.0 - gets a personal Home at /home, grouped by the action they must take, with rows that lead with the site rather than three internal ids. /incidents/:id becomes the only record page, with assessment, technical form, evidence, site and history as five tabs (three visible plus More on phones); no backend object is renamed and no state transition changes. Navigation collapses to at most four destinations per role, rendered as a bottom bar on phones, an 80px labelled rail with 12px labels on iPads and a 256px sidebar on desktops. Every hand-off, decision and irreversible step is a route-backed guided flow that is a full page below md and a centred dialog from md - one implementation, one breakpoint - stating its consequence before the button, holding that action's note, and leaving a receipt. Layout is composed per width against measured numbers rather than assumed from breakpoints: the third region on the form and case file is container-queried at 1240px of workspace, because main measures 1097px on a 1440 laptop with the sidebar pinned.
borrowed: proposal-case-file.json - the one-record-page backbone and the tab model, cut from seven tabs to five and relabelled by job (Who has it, Technical form) because 'Assessment' and 'Form' are the app's worst vocabulary collision
proposal-task-first.json - route-backed guided flows, the one-banner-one-primary-no-redirection law, never disabling a primary, and consequence-then-receipt on every workflow action

proposal-map-first.json - the map engineering only (popup-first with an explicit Open, never goTo on a poll tick, plot incidents by default, route-alias search, a list equivalent for every map interaction); its layer-chip model and map-as-home backbone are rejected on the record

proposal-progressive.json - relocate the GISA card bodies intact rather than re-authoring the 1,335-line page, the updated_at precondition against mobile offline drafts, the status-chip popover help mechanic (restricted here to detail pages), and the cross-client label-mirroring risk
proposal-summaries.json - the read-view SummaryList that replaces a disabled editing canvas for reviewers
spec-responsive.json, spec-data.json, spec-language.json - the pattern ladder, the essential/secondary/hidden discipline, and the one-name-per-object vocabulary table

judge-new-user.json, judge-field-tablet.json, judge-domain.json, judge-engineering.json - the four-criterion reviews that produced the 34.3/34.5 dead heat and the corrections (five tabs not seven, Records keeps both segments, keep Tailwind's breakpoints, iPad portrait gets a stated composition)

brief-core.md, brief-screens.md, brief-research.md - every measurement, every screen's data classification, and the outside research on work queues, responsive density, map/field UX, learnability and long forms
keyDecisions: R1 - Gave the Maintenance Field Reporter a real Home with three groups (Needs your update / Filed and waiting / Recently accepted), plus nav (Home + My reports) and persona rows; v1.0's single-home claim was false for one of seven personas.

R2 - Added SS7.19 'Update your report' at /incidents/:id/update as a route-backed flow with the coordinator's note quoted, a checklist of exactly the requested fields and non-requested fields shown read-only. Verified it needs NO backend work: PATCH /incidents/{id} (incidents.py:1408) exists, is scoped to the reporting user, and rejects out-of-scope edits (incidents.py:1444-1478).

R3 - Fixed the phone map height: /map keeps its bottom nav bar, so the map is calc(100svh - --header-h - --segment-h - --bottom-nav-h - env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); added --bottom-nav-h, --action-bar-h and --segment-h to the measured-variable list.

R4 - Resolved stacked bars with a general rule: a route shows either the bottom nav bar or one action bar, never both. On /terrain the action bar replaces the nav bar and the header gains a Home control; every full-height calc subtracts every bar on its route.

R5 - Re-costed the three-region desktop form against the measured 1097px main at 1440. The third region is now container-queried at 1240px of workspace (index 200 + form 720 + pane 320 + gaps = 1288), with the measured outcomes at 1280/1440/1600 stated; the sidebar defaults to the rail on form and case-file routes.

R6 - Stated the team (2 FE, 1 BE at a third time, designer at half, QA at half from Phase 3) and itemised every phase as component-days + assembly + QA divided by two engineers: 137 FE-days and 22.75 BE-days over 71 calendar days. Phase 0 rises from 10 to 14 days to match the 21.5 component-days its own scope assigns it.

R7 - Moved the feature flag to a build-time Vite variable (VITE_ERIS_UI_FLAGS, matching config.ts:15-22) and removed it from the backend critical path, because parse_user_metadata (user_metadata.py:44-48) whitelists three keys and drops the rest.
R8 - Added B11: GET/PUT /users/me/ui-preferences plus last_sign_in_at, for the nine 'once per account' promises that had nothing but localStorage behind them on shared field iPads.

R9 - Added B12 (Home queue filters) and moved it to Phase 1, the phase Home ships: CONSULTED in the reviewer queue with its assignment_role (assessments.py:828 excludes it today), plus reviewer_needed, ready_to_close, recently_done and the reporter's three groups. Four Home groups previously had no data source.

R10 - Added B14 for workflow_tree.py:40's 'Maintenance Field Worker' display string, with the client's roleLabel() re-mapping node role codes from Phase 2 so the tree is correct before the backend string changes.

R11 - Completed the workflow-node table to all eight statuses from workflow_tree.py:26-33 with label and per-role next-step copy; six were unmapped and would have failed Phase 0's own zero-raw-codes gate.

R12 - Added /submissions/:id?section=terrain to the route map (the mobile app's only link into the web 3D scene, mobile/.../[id].tsx:5056) mapped to ?panel=terrain3d with the old parameter kept as a permanent alias, and put the mobile string change in Phase 6.
R13 - Kept a real Not Found screen (SS7.20) showing the failed URL with one role-aware primary, rendering for anonymous users too; HomeRedirect is now for Login and RoleRoute denial only.

openQuestions: Does signing off close the incident? Today FINALIZED leaves it open until /incidents/{id}/resolve, and the workflow tree shows Resolution as CURRENT owned by the engineer. Auto-resolving is a one-line backend change that removes a step from every journey.
Can more than one assessment exist per incident? The case file assumes one; if a re-assessment can be opened, 'Who has it' needs a selector and the progress rail needs a branch.

Is the submission attachment endpoint callable from the browser origin today (CORS + presign), or is that B8? Until it is, the plan says in writing that photos come from the mobile app - and the engineer's first-day journey still ends one step short on an iPad browser.
Event Group vs Project on mobile: change the mobile strings in the same release, or ship 'Event Group (formerly Project)' for one release?

The legacy REVIEWER account role grants real authority today (SubmissionDetailPage.tsx:161, roleModel.ts:17-24). Deprecate and migrate the accounts, or keep the role with the explanatory empty state specified here?
A district with no DISTRICT_COORDINATOR strands reports UNASSIGNED with no notification. The System-health strip surfaces it - should ERIS also refuse the report, or notify a fallback?
Who may add a reviewer? Should the assigned engineer be able to propose one when review is blocked?
Theme and density on shared field iPads persist per browser, so the last person's theme wins. B11 moves them to the user record - confirm that is wanted before Phase 6 spends 1.5 backend days on it.
How long should 'Recently done by me' stay? The plan uses 7 days; B12 takes the window as a parameter, so this is a copy decision.
Do we keep three themes? Each triples the contrast verification surface, and dropping Coastal would measurably cut Phase 6.
Does last_sign_in_at exist on the user record? B11 adds it to /auth/me; if it does not exist, the 60-day return path becomes a schema change.
Emergency escalation: nothing marks an incident urgent, so every queue sorts by age. A severity flag is a backend field and a new chip - decide before Phase 1 sets the sort.

Should a non-assigned engineer keep the edit access they have today? canEdit is currently any FIELD_WORKER or ADMIN on a DRAFT/REJECTED submission with no assignment check; the plan narrows it to the assigned engineer, and it is unverified whether the server rejects the narrowed case.
How big is the 3D terrain payload? No evidence file measures it, so the unsourced 'about 20 MB' was removed from user-facing copy; Phase 4 measures it on the field iPad and puts a real number back.
